claims.authors: Jonathan Mark Kenoyer; J. Mark Kenoyer and Richard H. Meadow
claims.locations: 2006 Ravi/Kot Diji/Harappa sections; 2010 Table 1, PDF pp. 2–4
claims.claim: An early Harappa mark tradition develops toward the urban Indus system.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Excavated Ravi and Kot Diji marked sherds, early seals/sealings, Mature phase inscriptions; one site has a stratified sequence.
claims.missing: Specimen-level feature trajectories and frequency counts within subphases; extension from this pre-urban sequence to later South Asian scripts is not established.
claims.assessment: Chronological local development is testable with existing reports. Post-urban diagnostic continuity remains unverified.

claims.claim: Stepped-cross and related geometric seal motifs persist from Mehrgarh through Indus and late/Pirak contexts; transmitted ritual significance is suggested.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Mehrgarh phase seals, Mature seals, Jhukar-style geometric seals and Pirak Period II/IIIA examples.
claims.missing: Rare diagnostic structure, continuous dated distribution, and a null controlling the commonness of symmetric geometric forms. Ritual meaning is an interpretation.
claims.assessment: A route for motif comparison exists; it does not yet provide a transmitted writing system.

claims.authors: B. B. Lal; related comparisons by S. R. Rao and B. K. Thapar
claims.locations: Lal pp. 21–24; Rao pp. 128–137; Thapar pp. 66–68
claims.claim: Megalithic graffiti share many signs with Harappan and post-Harappan Chalcolithic pottery; Gujarat and central/Deccan cultures supply possible intermediates.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Lothal B, Rangpur IIC/III; Navdatoli, Prakash, Gilund/Ahar and Bahal/Tekwada; megalithic pottery and burial/ceramic comparisons.
claims.missing: Dated specimen series, fixed matching tolerances, independent annotations and complexity-matched chance inventory. Lal's 47 shared types compare with a pooled earlier repertoire, not the Indus script alone.
claims.assessment: Original arithmetic: 47/(47+6) and 47/(47+8). Chronology is uneven; cultural similarity is not a specimen-level mark chain.

claims.authors: S. R. Rao as discussed by Sundaresh and A. S. Gaur; integrity challenged by Vibha Tripathi
claims.claim: Two inscribed sherds and a composite-animal shell seal are related to late Indus material.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Ceramic comparisons with Rangpur/Lothal and an animal motif compared with Mohenjo-daro; unjoined pottery TL.
claims.missing: Dated stratigraphic context for these objects and legible diagnostic character sequence; proposed readings have no authentication.
claims.assessment: The report expressly lacks a definite dated shell context. These finds cannot close a calendar gap here.

claims.claim: Late Harappan Phase II seals and pottery inscriptions, plus one Phase III sherd, preserve Indus-type characters.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Two seals and four sherds in Phase II, one sherd in Phase III; trenches/layers and houses reported.
claims.missing: Modern calibration and a re-audit of residuality; continuation from these examples through Malwa/Jorwe into megalithic/Brahmi material.
claims.assessment: Seven catalogued inscriptions across two phases are concrete observations. Old conventional and MASCA brackets must remain separate.

claims.claim: Four marks on the Sulur dish can be paired with Indus signs and interpreted using Indus pair frequencies.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Sulur museum specimen 1935.4-19.15 and selected Indus tablet/sign pairs; no dated intervening assemblages supplied.
claims.missing: Independently dated intermediate pairs, a preregistered orientation rule and a search-space/chance correction. The comparison uses opposite tablet faces; the dish pairs are adjacent.
claims.assessment: Museum's first-century BCE label places the dish outside this package's 200 BCE endpoint. Pairing is a hypothesis, not a dated bridge.

claims.claim: Morphological and positional similarities relate Tamil Nadu graffiti to Indus signs; graffiti and Tamil-Brahmi are treated as parallel systems.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Large illustrated Tamil Nadu catalogue; cited Chalcolithic intermediates and older Lal/Mahadevan comparisons; Kilnamandi and other reported dated contexts.
claims.missing: Specimen-to-deposit-to-sample table for early marks, dated frequency series, declared allograph/match rules, and complexity/context nulls. Early unmarked Sivagalai urn dates supply no graffiti intermediate.
claims.assessment: The 2025 accessible witness is an eight-page brochure. Percentage denominators differ across base signs, variants, composites, Indus graffiti and script corpora.

claims.authors: K. Rajan and R. Sivanantham; earlier positions reviewed by Richard Salomon
claims.claim: Several excavated contexts are proposed to place Tamil-Brahmi before Ashoka.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Porunthal inscribed ringstands associated with rice; Kodumanal dated settlement levels; Keeladi occupation samples; Sivagalai charcoal context.
claims.missing: Original calibration outputs and exact registered sherd/ringstand-to-sample joins in this assembled record. Porunthal's 490/450 BCE labels are conventional BP conversions, not calibrated intervals.
claims.assessment: Assess each association independently. Early Tamil-Brahmi would constrain early historic chronology; it would not by itself establish Indus transmission.

claims.authors: R. A. E. Coningham, F. R. Allchin, C. M. Batt and D. Lucy; S. U. Deraniyagala
claims.locations: 1996 abstract; Deraniyagala Early Historic writing section; Salomon p. 12
claims.claim: Anuradhapura pottery supports early Brahmi and suggests transmission associated with merchants; published date assessments differ.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Excavated inscribed sherds with stratigraphic/radiometric investigation; author overview also reports TL checks.
claims.missing: Full 1996 sample tables, laboratory identifiers, images and depositional join audit in this package; no mark chain back to late Indus.
claims.assessment: Beginning-fourth-century and 600–500 BCE assessments are stored separately and attributed.

claims.claim: Origin proposals include indigenous invention, Indus derivation, several Semitic prototypes, Aramaic adaptation and a Mauryan mixed invention.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Indus theories use sign resemblances; Semitic theories use letter forms/system structure; adaptation models invoke historical contact and Indian phonological organization.
claims.missing: Directly dated stages of Brahmi formation. Resemblance alone needs null controls; a contact route needs actual intermediate inscriptions.
claims.assessment: Cunningham/Ojha/Pandey: indigenous proposals; Langdon/Hunter and aspects of Sircar: Indus comparisons; Bühler: northern Semitic/Phoenician; Taylor: southern Semitic; Falk 1993: deliberate Greek/Kharosthi combination; Salomon: Aramaic most likely, with Indian phonological adaptation and objections to Greek vowel derivation. Original works were not opened here; these are attributed through Salomon.

claims.authors: Richard Salomon reviewing Bühler and later scholarship
claims.claim: Kharosthi is derived from Aramaic, with disputed timing and adaptation details.
claims.intermediate_evidence: Systematic letter and writing-system comparisons and Achaemenid historical setting; earliest recovered historical endpoint is Ashokan Shahbazgarhi/Mansehra.
claims.missing: Directly dated formative Kharosthi corpus; early coin countermarks proposed by Rapson were questioned and are not used as a pre-Mauryan endpoint.
claims.assessment: Provides an adjacent-region adaptation comparator for tests; no inference of Indus phonetic values follows.
